articles.title: Ozempic, Zepbound and other GLP-1 drugs will carry a warning about a rare vision loss condition. An expert puts the risk in perspective.
articles.summary: GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Zepbound may slightly raise the risk of a rare eye condition that can cause vision loss. But for most people, the benefits still...
articles.body:
GLP-1 medications may slightly increase the risk of a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced on Nov. 9, 2026. The agency will now require GLP-1 drugs — including Ozempic, Zepbound and 10 others — to carry a warning about the potential risk of vision loss on their labels.

The condition, called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION, is extremely uncommon, regardless of GLP-1 use. But clinical trials suggest that there's enough increased risk to merit a warning.

It doesn't mean that anyone taking a GLP-1 should stop — the chances of developing NAION are still very low, an expert tells Yahoo. But it is worth knowing what NAION is, who's at greatest risk and the signs to watch out for.

NAION is the most common type of ischemic optic neuropathy , a condition in which reduced blood flow damages the optic nerve, the primary pathway responsible for vision. Without enough oxygen-rich blood, parts of the nerve start to die, which can lead to permanent vision loss.

It's exceedingly rare, affecting roughly 2 to 10 out of every 100,000 adults ages 50 or older in the U.S. each year, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO). It's even less likely among younger people, who make up between 6% and 23% of U.S. cases.

NAION primarily develops in one eye. It's usually painless, but it comes on suddenly — typically in a matter of minutes or hours, Chintan Dave , an associate professor of pharmacy and epidemiology at the Institute for Health and the Ernest Mario School of Pharmacy at Rutgers University, tells Yahoo.

While someone's vision may never return to its former state, the condition rarely causes blindness. Instead, "you just get blind spots, so you lose a part of your vision; it can often be in the upper or lower half of the visual field" of one eye, explains Dave.

It's not clear what exactly causes NAION, regardless of whether someone has taken GLP-1 medications, says Dave, who has studied the relationship between the eye condition and the medications. But there are some known risk factors, many of which overlap with health conditions that GLP-1 drugs can help to manage. They include:

Type 2 diabetes (although NAION is not to be confused with diabetic retinopathy )

Men, he notes, are also more likely than women to develop NAION.

There are no known treatments for NAION. But, because underlying health problems — including high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes — that can lead to NAION pose additional risks, it's important to seek medical attention anyway, says Dave. About 15% of people who have NAION in one eye eventually develop it in the other, according to the Cleveland Clinic .

Because the condition is so uncommon, there's little data on how likely it is to resolve or worsen, Dave says. The AAO estimates that after the onset of NAION, about 70% of people will see no further changes to their vision; 20% may experience modest improvements, and the blind spots worsen for about 10% of patients.

Dave and his colleagues found that there were between 3 and 4 more cases of NAION per 10,000 people taking GLP-1 medications than among those taking other diabetes medications over an 18-month period.

In its own analysis , the FDA found that there were 6.4 cases of NAION among every 100,000 people taking GLP-1 drugs annually, compared with 3.8 cases per year among people taking placebos or other blood sugar medications.

What is it about GLP-1 treatments that might increase the likelihood of this vision loss condition? "NAION is so rare to begin with that we just don't have a really good sense of what could be the reason," says Dave. One theory, he says, is that rapid reductions in blood sugar levels may have some knock-on effect on smaller blood vessels like those that supply the optic nerve. But for now it's nothing more than a hypothesis.

Some people notice slight, temporary blurring of their vision before developing NAION, according to the AAO and Cleveland Clinic. Dave says that it's common for people with the condition to simply wake up and notice their vision is blurry. In either case, "immediately go to the emergency room," says Dave.

Even though there is no treatment, he says doctors may be able to help prevent NAION from worsening by reducing inflammation and addressing risk factors. Seeing a doctor is also important for ruling out other causes, per the AAO.

Dave stresses how unlikely it is to develop NAION, both in the general population and among GLP-1 users. Despite that, hundreds of patients have filed lawsuits against GLP-1 makers, claiming they developed the condition after taking the medications.

"The most important thing is to put the risk into perspective," he says. "GLPs have substantial real-world benefits in patients with diabetes, obesity or cardiovascular disease." While Dave's research found an increased risk of a potentially serious eye condition, "the absolute risk was very small," he says. "For most patients, the benefits of these medications will continue to far outweigh the risk."

articles.title: Família de casal esfaqueado no Centro de SP cobra por Justiça e quer saber motivação do crime: 'Queremos entender o que houve' | G1
articles.standfirst: Irmão de Erika Lima da Silva, de 41 anos, contesta informação inicial de que suspeito seria ex-namorado da vítima; ela é casada com Leandro Barbosa da Silva, de 42, há 20 anos. Ele morreu no ataque, e ela passou por cirurgia e está internada.
articles.summary: Irmão de Erika Lima da Silva, de 41 anos, contesta informação inicial de que suspeito seria ex-namorado da vítima; ela é casada com Leandro Barbosa da Silva, de 42, há 20 anos. Ele morreu no ataque, e ela passou por cirurgia e está internada.
articles.body:
A família de Erika Lima da Silva, de 41 anos, e Leandro Barbosa da Silva, de 42, quer respostas sobre o ataque a facadas que deixou o homem morto e a mulher ferida em frente a uma casa de shows na Avenida Nove de Julho, na Bela Vista, no Centro de São Paulo . Uma câmera de segurança registrou o momento do crime (veja acima).

Ao g1 , o irmão da mulher, Eudes da Silva Lima Junior, diz que os parentes não receberam informações sobre o suspeito nem sobre a motivação do crime e cobram por justiça.

"Minha sobrinha foi à delegacia e não recebeu nenhuma informação. Não nos disseram quem é o suspeito e queremos saber o que houve, queremos justiça, queremos entender o que motivou para esse crime horrível. Minha família merece", disse.

Eudes ainda contesta a informação inicial da investigação de que o suspeito seria um ex-namorado de Erika. Segundo ele, a mulher e Leandro eram casados havia 20 anos e tinham dois filhos.

"Minha irmã é casada com o Leandro há 20 anos. Eles têm dois filhos e são da Zona Norte. Não acredito que o assassino seja um ex-namorado. Desconheço sobre desavença com alguém. Eles estão juntos há anos. Por isso, queremos entender se foi uma briga e quem é esse assassino. Queremos Justiça", afirmou.

Segundo Eudes, Erika trabalha em uma empresa de ônibus, enquanto Leandro trabalhava montando estandes. Ele ressalta que os dois foram para a festa comemorar, mas que a família ficou sabendo do crime pela imprensa.

"Eu vi a notícia pela imprensa cedo e fiquei horrorizado. Primeiro vi sobre os corpos e até pensei: que horror o corpo ali. Eu nem imaginava que se tratava do meu cunhado. Depois, meio-dia, meu companheiro me ligou, disse que a imprensa tinha dado os nomes das vítimas e pediu para eu ser forte, que ia me levar ao hospital onde minha irmã estava", relatou.

Homem é morto a facadas e mulher fica ferida em frente a casa de shows no Centro de SP — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Erika foi encaminhada à Santa Casa, passou por uma cirurgia por ter sido atingida no abdômen e, segundo o irmão, está estável. Leandro, porém, não resistiu aos ferimentos. Eudes também questionou a demora no atendimento ao cunhado. Segundo ele, o homem ficou horas esperando por socorro.

"Se aconteceu durante a madrugada e recebeu atendimento só de manhã, por que não fizeram algo de emergência no local? Por que a casa não ajudou a socorrer? Por que o corpo ficou lá? São muitas perguntas ainda sem respostas", ressaltou.

Até a noite desta segunda-feira (9), o corpo de Leandro ainda estava no Instituto Médico Legal (IML) e não havia sido liberado para a família. Enquanto Erika permanecia internada na Santa Casa, os parentes também aguardavam informações sobre a liberação do corpo.

O g1 questionou a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP) sobre a falta de informações relatada pelos familiares, a identificação do suspeito e a linha de investigação sobre a motivação do crime. A pasta foi procurada e aguarda-se retorno.

articles.title: Dois trabalhadores morrem após levarem choque e caírem de prédio em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Eles chegaram a ser levados ao hospital, mas não resistiram aos ferimentos.
articles.summary: Eles chegaram a ser levados ao hospital, mas não resistiram aos ferimentos.
articles.body:
Dois homens que trabalhavam na fachada de um prédio em Balneário Camboriú , no Litoral Norte de Santa Catarina , morreram após levarem choque elétrico e caírem. Eles chegaram a ser levados ao hospital, mas não resistiram aos ferimentos.

O acidente ocorreu no final da tarde de segunda-feira (9). Eles trabalhavam para uma empresa terceirizada, que não teve o nome divulgado.

O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar foi chamado às 17h34. O acidente ocorreu no Centro da cidade.

Ao chegarem ao local, os socorristas isolaram a área. Os dois trabalhadores estavam caídos na rua em parada cardiorrespiratória, com traumatismo cranioencefálico, sinais de descarga elétrica e hemorragia.

Moradores que presenciaram o acidente contaram aos bombeiros que os trabalhadores eram de uma empresa terceirizada e faziam um serviço na fachada de um prédio, usando material de alumínio composto.

Eles levantavam uma peça desse material, através de uma escada, para o telhado do edifício quando sofreram a descarga elétrica, vinda de uma rede de alta tensão.

Bombeiros em atendimento a trabalhadores que caíram de prédio após choque elétrico em Balneário Camboriú — Foto: CBMSC/Divulgação

Um dos trabalhadores caiu do telhado, de uma altura de cerca de 6 metros. O outro, que estava na escada, sofreu uma queda de aproximadamente 3 metros.

Os bombeiros fizeram manobras de ressuscitação cardiopulmonar e reanimação com desfibrilador. Os dois trabalhadores foram levados ao Hospital Ruth Cardoso, em Balneário Camboriú, pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU). Porém, não resistiram aos ferimentos.

articles.title: Adolescente atingida por árvore durante temporal em SP tem melhora | G1
articles.standfirst: Atualização divulgada por familiares na tarde desta terça-feira (10) aponta redução do inchaço no cérebro e evolução pulmonar. Ela sofreu traumatismo e teve pé reconstruído em cirurgia.
articles.summary: Ela sofreu traumatismo e teve pé reconstruído em cirurgia.
articles.body:
A adolescente de 14 anos atingida por uma árvore durante um temporal em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP) no último sábado (7) apresentou melhora clínica, informou a família dela na tarde desta terça-feira (10).

Segundo a atualização, um exame realizado na segunda (9) mostrou redução do inchaço no cérebro da adolescente, sem sangramento.

Além disso, ainda de acordo com os familiares, o pulmão da menina também melhorou. Nesta quarta (11), os médicos devem começar a diminuir o sedativo para ver como ela irá reagir.

A queda da árvore sobre a adolescente foi no Parque dos Ipês, principal parque da cidade. A vítima passou por uma cirurgia na cabeça após sofrer um traumatismo e também precisou ter um dos pés reconstruídos por conta das lesões causadas pelo acidente.

Ela permanece internada no Hospital Estadual de Sumaré (SP).

Árvores caídas no Parque dos Ipês, em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, onde uma jovem de 14 anos estava quando foi atingida — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Para acelerar a recuperação da cidade após os estragos, cerca de 23 equipes atuam em diferentes regiões.

A força-tarefa recebeu reforços de equipes da Defesa Civil de Indaiatuba, do DER e, nesta terça-feira, também da Defesa Civil de Americana. A expectativa da prefeitura é de que os trabalhos de limpeza e reorganização levem mais de uma semana.

Os trabalhos de limpeza e restauração na cidade devem durar cerca de uma semana, informou a Defesa Civil.

As árvores caíram sobre vias, muros e fiações elétricas com as fortes chuvas e rajadas de ventos, entre 60 e 100 quilômetros por hora.

"Acredito que vamos levar uma semana para deixar a cidade em ordem", estima o secretário de Segurança, Trânsito e Defesa Civil, Rômulo Gobbi.

Também foram registrados danos em telhados, queda de fiação e pontos de alagamento.

O Parque dos Ipês está fechado para trabalhos de limpeza e avaliação de estragos. Segundo a Defesa Civil, mais de 20 árvores caíram dentro de ao redor do parque. Equipes da prefeitura fazem remoção de galhos e manutenção.

Ao todo, foram registradas ocorrências em mais de 150 locais da cidade.

articles.title: O que pode explicar 500 árvores caídas em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste | G1
articles.standfirst: Total de ocorrências envolvendo árvores em único dia foi o maior em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP) nos últimos 15 anos. Equipes de municípios da região mobilizam força-tarefa.
articles.summary: Total de ocorrências desse tipo em único dia foi o maior na cidade nos últimos 15 anos.
articles.body:
Diferentes fatores podem explicar a queda de ao menos 500 árvores durante o temporal que atingiu Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP) no último sábado.

O total de ocorrências envolvendo árvores em um único dia foi o maior da cidade nos últimos 15 anos.

Diante disso, equipes de vários municípios da região mobilizaram uma força-tarefa para realizar a limpeza e restauração de mais de 150 pontos atingidos ( veja abaixo detalhes ).

A tempestade teve início por volta das 15h do último sábado e durou menos de meia hora, mas foi suficiente para registrar 37,3 milímetros (mm) de chuva e rajadas de vento de até 100 km/h.

Allan Jonas Duarte, engenheiro ambiental, destaca os plantios inadequados, idade das árvores e as mudanças climáticas como potenciais fatores para explicar a frequência de ocorrências desse tipo nas cidades.

"Possuímos nos nossos municípios muitas árvores plantadas inadequadamente. Muitas árvores que deveriam possuir área permeável maior, principalmente árvores com raízes superficiais. São espécies inapropriadas para serem plantadas em calçadas, por exemplo."

Temporal derrubou ao menos 500 árvores em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Um dos locais afetados foi o Parque dos Ipês, principal parque da cidade, onde cerca de 20 árvores caíram. Uma delas atingiu uma adolescente de 14 anos, que passou por cirurgia e permanece internada em estado grave, porém estável, no Hospital Estadual de Sumaré (SP).

Sobre a saúde das espécies, Duarte pontuou a necessidade das podas regulares, o que poderia diminuir riscos, segundo ele.

"Temos as árvores das cidades envelhecendo. A saúde dessa árvore está fragilizada por fungos, principalmente. Ela parece estar saudável, mas é uma árvore que está, por dentro, fragilizada. Fazer uma poda adequada para arborização urbana para que a gente consiga minimizar esse impacto mecânico do vento na copa, fazendo que o vento corte a árvore, e não a derrube."

Por fim, para o engenheiro ambiental, o cenário deve ser visto como um alerta para as mudanças climáticas.

"Esse recorde de queda de árvore é um alerta para as mudanças climáticas. O caminho não é tirar as árvores indiscriminadamente, mas investir no manejo preventivo, substituir as espécies doentes por espécies nativas ou espécies adequadas mais resistentes e fazer as podas que irão ajudar as árvores a cortarem esses ventos, sem caírem."

"Acredito que vamos levar uma semana para deixar a cidade em ordem", estima o secretário de Segurança, Trânsito e Defesa Civil, Rômulo Gobbi.

Também foram registrados danos em telhados, queda de fiação e pontos de alagamento.

articles.title: Médico achado morto em depósito de esterco procurou ajuda em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Polícia Civil acredita que José Augusto Nogueira Ribas tenha tentado buscar ajuda na propriedade rural onde foi encontrado morto. Corpo foi localizado após sucção e remoção de dejetos.
articles.summary: Propriedade onde ele foi encontrado morto não era da família dele, confirmou delegado.
articles.body:
A Polícia Civil acredita que o médico Augusto Nogueira Ribas, de 30 anos, tenha ido procurar ajuda na propriedade rural onde foi encontrado morto em Xanxerê , no Oeste de Santa Catarina . Segundo o delegado regional, Vinícius Iunes, ela havia atolado o carro na estrada.

Ribas estava desaparecido desde a madrugada segunda-feira (8). O corpo dele foi encontrado em um depósito de esterco, na tarde de segunda (9), após sucção e remoção de dejetos.

O delegado destacou que a propriedade rural onde o corpo foi encontrado, na localidade de Linha Passo Trancado, não é de familiares do médico. O carro dele, um Cruze, foi encontrado perto do local.

A Polícia Civil aguarda a conclusão dos exames periciais e demais investigações para poder precisar as circunstâncias da morte.

Conforme avaliação pericial preliminar, o corpo não apresentava sinais externos visíveis de violência ou indícios imediatos de ação homicida. A hipótese de morte acidental figura, inicialmente, entre as possibilidades consideradas.

Médico de 30 anos foi achado morto em depósito de esterco em Xanxerê (SC) — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação e Redes sociais/Reprodução

Corpo foi encontrado após sucção e remoção de dejetos

O corpo de José foi localizado pelos bombeiros, acionados na madrugada para fazer buscas na comunidade. O local fica na Zona Rural de Xanxerê.

A equipe ouviu testemunhas e fez buscas preliminares na região até as 5h, sem sucesso.

Às 8h de segunda, após a suspeita de que ele pudesse estar dentro do depósito, houve a sucção e a remoção dos dejetos acumulados e o corpo foi achado. A estrutura tem cerca de 3 metros de profundidade.

De acordo com os bombeiros, o volume retirado equivale a mais de oito caminhões-tanque de dejetos, com capacidade aproximada de 20 mil litros cada.

Corpo de médico foi encontrado em propriedade rural de Xanxerê (SC) — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

José Augusto Nogueira Ribas trabalhava em um dos principais hospitais da região. Ele foi descrito pelos colegas de trabalho como um profissional dedicado e querido pelos pacientes.

Conhecido como Guto, ele atuava como clínico-geral no Hospital Regional do Oeste e na Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) de Chapecó , maior cidade da região e vizinha a Xanxerê.

Médico José Augusto Nogueira Ribas foi encontrado morto em Xanxerê — Foto: Reprodução

"Profissional dedicado, era muito querido por seus pacientes e colegas, sendo reconhecido por sua humanidade, atenção e compromisso com o cuidado ao próximo. Uma pessoa amada por todos, que deixa uma marca de respeito e carinho por onde passou", escreveu a administração da UPA.

No hospital, o profissional atuava desde 2025. O velório ocorreu na manhã desta terça-feira (10), na Capela da Central de Luto, com sepultamento logo depois, no Cemitério Municipal de Xanxerê.

A Secretaria de Estado da Saúde e a Associação Hospitalar Lenoir Vargas Ferreira (ALVF) manifestam profundo pesar pelo falecimento do Dr. José Augusto Nogueira Ribas, confirmado na tarde desta segunda (9), no município de Xanxerê.

Excelente profissional e querido colega, Guto, como era carinhosamente chamado, fez parte da equipe do Hospital Regional do Oeste desde janeiro de 2025, deixando sua contribuição e uma trajetória marcada pelo cuidado, profissionalismo e pelas relações construídas ao longo de sua caminhada na instituição.

Neste momento de dor, nos solidarizamos com seus familiares, amigos e colegas, desejando força e conforto a todos.

articles.title: A Clínica: Série do Globoplay revela traumas de famosos em Atibaia | G1
articles.standfirst: Episódios reúnem depoimentos de artistas e outros ex-pacientes sobre tratamentos na clínica Maxwell, em Atibaia (SP), marcada por questionamentos sobre os métodos do psiquiatra Sabino Ferreira de Farias Neto.
articles.summary: A série A Clínica, do Globoplay, apresenta relatos de Rafael Ilha e outros ex-pacientes sobre tratamentos polêmicos e mortes na instituição Maxwell, em Atibaia.
articles.body:
A série documental "A Clínica", dos Estúdios Globo, reúne relatos de ex-pacientes que passaram pela clínica psiquiátrica Maxwell, em Atibaia, no interior de São Paulo. Nos seis episódios, pessoas conhecidas do público contam experiências vividas durante tratamentos conduzidos pelo médico Sabino Ferreira de Farias Neto, incluindo dificuldades para deixar a instituição, uso de medicamentos e situações que classificam como traumáticas .

Entre os relatos está o do cantor Rafael Ilha, que começou a usar cocaína aos 15 anos e desenvolveu dependência química. Segundo ele, o vício o levou do sucesso nos palcos às ruas de São Paulo.

"A principal coisa que a droga arranca de você é o teu amor próprio. A primeira coisa", afirma.

Rafael conta que, durante o período de dependência, chegou a pedir um cobertor à mãe porque dormia no chão e sentia frio. Mais tarde, foi encaminhado à clínica Maxwell, que prometia atendimento humanizado e tinha aparência de hotel de luxo.

Rafael Ilha, Maurício Mattar e Deborah Blando estão entre os artistas que também foram pacientes da clínica. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo/Fantástico

O cantor afirma que, depois de um ano internado, quis deixar a instituição, mas não conseguiu. Em uma tentativa de sair, chegou a engolir três isqueiros, uma pilha e uma caneta .

Em outro momento, ao manifestar que queria ir embora para usar drogas, Rafael diz que um funcionário pegou a chave de um carro e permitiu que ele saísse e voltasse.

Relatos de ex-pacientes e morte durante tratamento

A série também apresenta o caso do lutador Ryan Gracie, que morreu em 2007 durante um tratamento com Sabino Ferreira. A irmã dele afirma que, segundo o laudo do Instituto Médico Legal (IML), a morte foi provocada pela medicação administrada pelo médico.

"Não sou eu que tô dizendo, é o IML", diz Flávia Gracie.

Sabino Ferreira foi condenado em primeira instância, mas acabou absolvido pelo Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo. O médico também participa da série documental e apresenta sua versão dos acontecimentos.

O cantor Rafael Ilha, ex-integrante do grupo Polegar, ficou internado na clínica psiquiátrica. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo/Fantástico

A produção reúne ainda relatos de outros ex-pacientes sobre o uso de medicamentos e as condições de permanência na clínica. Uma das pessoas ouvidas conta que recebeu a orientação de que seria medicada para não querer deixar a instituição.

Segundo os produtores, os depoimentos mostram a relação ambígua que alguns pacientes mantinham com o médico: ao mesmo tempo que pareciam admirá-lo, também relatavam experiências traumáticas.

Investigação começou com documentário sobre Anita Harley

O ponto de partida para a produção foi a história de uma mulher que estava internada havia 25 anos na clínica, sem contato com parentes. O caso apareceu durante as gravações de "O testamento, o segredo de Anita Harley", outro documentário realizado pela mesma equipe.

A investigação sobre Anita Harley, que estava em coma havia dez anos, levou os produtores a conhecer a história da sobrinha dela e a questionar os motivos pelos quais a mulher permanecia internada havia tanto tempo.

A partir daí, a equipe passou a investigar outros personagens ligados à clínica e a reunir relatos sobre as experiências vividas na instituição.

Série sobre Anita Harley foi o ponto de partida para o novo documentário do Globoplay. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A série também traz uma entrevista com Sabino Ferreira. Segundo um dos responsáveis pela produção, o médico resistiu a participar, mas a equipe insistiu na importância de ouvir sua versão.

Questionado sobre o que um documentário a respeito dele e da clínica não poderia deixar de mostrar, Sabino respondeu: "A verdade".

"A Clínica" tem seis episódios e estreia no Globoplay. Na televisão, a produção vai ao ar às segundas e quartas-feiras, depois da novela "Quem Ama Cuida".

O podcast Isso É Fantástico está disponível no g1 e nos principais aplicativos de podcasts, trazendo grandes reportagens, investigações e histórias fascinantes em podcast com o selo de jornalismo do Fantástico: profundidade, contexto e informação. Siga, curta ou assine o Isso É Fantástico no seu tocador de podcasts favorito. Todo domingo tem um episódio novo.

articles.title: A história do reencontro entre pai e Gracyanne Barbosa antes de morte | G1
articles.standfirst: O reencontro aconteceu em agosto deste ano, em Brasilândia (MS) no Dia dos Pais. Elias Barbosa enfretava o câncer de próstata desde 2020.
articles.summary: O reencontro aconteceu em agosto deste ano, em Brasilândia (MS) no Dia dos Pais. Elias Barbosa enfretava o câncer de próstata desde 2020.
articles.body:
Gracyanne Barbosa e o pai Elias barbosa, em 2021, — Foto: Redes Sociais

Três meses antes da morte do pai, a influenciadora e modelo Gracyanne Barbosa se reconciliou com ele durante uma visita a Brasilândia . Elias Barbosa enfrentava um câncer de próstata desde 2020 e morreu na noite de segunda-feira (9 ). O reencontro foi compartilhado pela influenciadora nas redes sociais, em agosto de 2026.

Ao g1 , a assessoria de Gracyanne informou que a influenciadora soube da morte do pai após participar de uma entrevista ao vivo com Blogueirinha, no Multishow. Segundo a equipe, ela segue recebendo apoio neste momento.

O motivo do afastamento entre pai e filha não foi divulgado. Na publicação feita após o reencontro, Gracyanne celebrou a reconciliação.

"Hoje foi um dia de amor, de reconciliação, de cura e, principalmente, de paz no coração. Eu acredito muito que Deus transforma aquilo que entregamos nas mãos Dele. Te amo pai. Feliz dia dos Pais", escreveu na ocasião.

Post feito por Gracyanne Barbosa ao pai Elias Barbosa, no Dia dos Pais — Foto: Redes sociais

O pai da influenciadora e modelo Gracyanne Barbosa, Elias Barbosa, morreu aos 72 anos, na noite de segunda-feira (9), enquanto estava internado no Hospital Regional de Brasilândia, em Mato Grosso do Sul. Segundo a funerária responsável pelo atendimento, ele tratava um câncer de próstata. O corpo será velado na cidade nesta terça-feira (10).

Três meses antes da morte, Gracyanne havia publicado uma homenagem ao pai nas redes sociais, no Dia dos Pais. Na ocasião, ela contou que os dois haviam se reconciliado e falou sobre amor, cura e paz.

“Hoje foi um dia de amor, de reconciliação, de cura e, principalmente, de paz no coração”, escreveu a influenciadora.

A assessoria de Gracyanne informou ao g1 que ela soube da morte logo após participar de uma entrevista ao vivo com Blogueirinha. Em nota, a equipe afirmou que este é um momento delicado e que a influenciadora está recebendo apoio.

articles.title: Hospital Regional de Oriximiná: 72 sessões de hemodiálise na UTI | G1
articles.standfirst: Serviço especializado implementado na unidade do oeste paraense já beneficiou 23 pacientes com comprometimento da função renal desde o mês de junho.
articles.summary: O Hospital Regional de Oriximiná assegura suporte de alta complexidade pelo SUS para pacientes com insuficiência renal, somando 72 sessões realizadas desde junho.
articles.body:
Hospital Regional de Oriximiná — Foto: Agência Pará

O Hospital Regional de Oriximiná Menino Jesus (HRMJ) tem assegurado suporte avançado de alta complexidade para pacientes internados na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) que necessitam de terapia de substituição renal. Dados divulgados pela unidade mostram que, entre os meses de junho e outubro, o serviço de hemodiálise já contabiliza 23 pacientes atendidos, totalizando 72 sessões realizadas.

A hemodiálise em ambiente de terapia intensiva desempenha um papel vital para filtrar e limpar o sangue de pacientes com disfunções renais agudas ou crônicas descompensadas, removendo toxinas, excesso de líquidos e mantendo o equilíbrio de minerais essenciais no organismo.

O médico intensivista José Fernando Mendes destacou a relevância da oferta do procedimento dentro da unidade no oeste do Pará para garantir a sobrevida e a estabilidade clínica de casos graves.

“É um serviço de extrema importância, que contribui para a qualidade de vida dos pacientes. Existe toda uma equipe multiprofissional empenhada nesse atendimento. Temos uma grande demanda, e a oferta desse serviço é fundamental para garantir a sobrevida da população”, explicou o médico.

A terapia dialítica na UTI é indicada tanto para quadros de insuficiência renal quanto para situações de urgência médica — como intoxicações, acidose metabólica e desequilíbrios eletrolíticos graves.

Para assegurar a segurança de cada procedimento, a equipe multiprofissional do HRMJ passou por capacitações específicas para monitoramento contínuo dos sinais vitais e do funcionamento dos cateteres durante as sessões.

Referência em atendimento de média e alta complexidade na região do Baixo Amazonas, o Hospital Regional de Oriximiná funciona exclusivamente pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). A estrutura da unidade conta com leitos de enfermaria, leitos de acolhimento inicial e UTI, além de suporte diagnóstico completo com exames de imagem (como tomografia e ultrassonografia) e análises laboratoriais.

articles.title: Hospital São José celebra 90 anos com missa em ação de graças na Catedral São José | G1
articles.standfirst: Celebração reuniu religiosas, autoridades, médicos, colaboradores, ex-profissionais e comunidade para marcar nove décadas de uma história iniciada pelas Irmãs Escolares de Nossa Senhora
articles.summary: Celebração reuniu religiosas, autoridades, médicos, colaboradores, ex-profissionais e comunidade para marcar nove décadas de uma história iniciada pelas Irmãs Escolares de Nossa Senhora
articles.body:
Uma história que começou com fé, coragem e uma missão de cuidar da vida foi celebrada neste domingo, 8 de novembro, em um momento especial de gratidão. O Hospital São José reuniu autoridades, religiosas, médicos, colaboradores, voluntários, benfeitores, ex-colaboradores, ex-médicos, representantes da comunidade e convidados na Catedral São José, em Criciúma, para a missa em ação de graças pelos seus 90 anos de história.

A celebração foi presidida pelo bispo da Diocese de Criciúma, Dom Jacinto Inácio Flach, e contou com a participação de padres da Diocese, além de representantes de diferentes setores da sociedade. O encontro marcou oficialmente as nove décadas da instituição, fundada em 8 de novembro de 1936, a partir da missão assumida pelas Irmãs Escolares de Nossa Senhora.

A escolha da Catedral São José para esse momento tem um significado especial. Há 90 anos, foi justamente naquela igreja que as religiosas, acompanhadas pela comunidade de Criciúma, participaram de uma celebração eucarística antes de seguirem em procissão até o hospital, onde assumiriam a missão de cuidar da saúde da população.

Missa em ação de graças na Catedral São José, em Criciúma, marcou os 90 anos do Hospital São José — Foto: Divulgação/Hospital São José

Ao recordar esse momento durante a missa, a diretora institucional do Hospital São José, Irmã Terezinha Buss, destacou a emoção de celebrar as nove décadas no mesmo local onde tudo começou.

“Que bonito recordar esta história, recordar este momento. Hoje, ao celebrarmos os 90 anos do hospital, nosso primeiro agradecimento é novamente a Deus, fonte da vida e de todo bem. Foi sua providência que nos sustentou, sua força que nos amparou nas dificuldades e seu amor que se fez presente pelo cuidado das mãos de tantas pessoas”, destacou.

Em sua mensagem, Irmã Terezinha também agradeceu às religiosas que iniciaram essa trajetória, às gerações de Irmãs que deram continuidade à missão e a todos que contribuíram para o desenvolvimento da instituição. A diretora institucional fez questão de reconhecer o trabalho de médicos, colaboradores, voluntários e profissionais de todos os setores, lembrando que cada atividade, mesmo aquelas realizadas longe da assistência direta, é parte fundamental do cuidado.

Celebração reuniu diferentes gerações que ajudaram a construir a história de cuidado e acolhimento do Hospital São José — Foto: Divulgação/Hospital São José

“Deus conhece cada plantão, cada esforço, cada renúncia e cada gesto de doação silenciosa. A palavra que acalma, as mãos que cuidam, o alimento preparado, o ambiente limpo, o trabalho organizado e a atenção que devolve esperança. Os frutos de sua dedicação permanecerão para sempre”, afirmou.

A religiosa também agradeceu às autoridades, aos parceiros, benfeitores e à comunidade, além de destacar a confiança dos pacientes e familiares, que dão sentido à missão do hospital. Em sua fala, recordou especialmente as Irmãs pioneiras, que aceitaram o desafio de assumir uma instituição hospitalar mesmo sem conhecer os desafios que encontrariam, confiando na providência divina e fazendo da própria vida uma doação.

Durante a celebração, Dom Jacinto também destacou a importância da missão assumida pelas Irmãs Escolares de Nossa Senhora e o significado social do Hospital São José ao longo dessas nove décadas. O bispo ressaltou o compromisso da instituição com o atendimento às pessoas mais vulneráveis, lembrando que o acesso à saúde e a um tratamento digno deve alcançar também aqueles que mais precisam.

Durante a missa, foram reconhecidas as contribuições de religiosas, profissionais, voluntários, benfeitores e da comunidade — Foto: Divulgação/Hospital São José

Dom Jacinto manifestou reconhecimento à congregação e às religiosas que mantêm viva essa missão, destacando a contribuição das Irmãs para a história da saúde em Criciúma e na região. Também parabenizou a instituição pela trajetória construída e pela dedicação de todos que fazem parte dela.

A missa foi um momento de encontro entre diferentes gerações que ajudaram a construir a história do Hospital São José. Estiveram presentes pessoas que acompanharam o crescimento da instituição, profissionais que dedicaram anos de trabalho, aqueles que hoje seguem atuando no cuidado e representantes da comunidade que, ao longo do tempo, confiaram no hospital.

A missa pelos 90 anos do Hospital São José celebrou o legado das Irmãs pioneiras e a dedicação de quem mantém viva a missão de cuidar da vida — Foto: Divulgação/Hospital São José

Fundado em 1936, o Hospital São José cresceu junto com Criciúma e se tornou referência em assistência hospitalar de média e alta complexidade para o Sul de Santa Catarina. Atualmente, atende uma população estimada em cerca de 1 milhão de pessoas, abrangendo 45 municípios das regiões da AMREC, AMESC e AMUREL.

Somente em 2025, foram realizados mais de 260 mil atendimentos. A instituição conta com mais de 1.700 colaboradores, além de médicos, residentes, estudantes e voluntários que contribuem diariamente para a assistência.

Ao longo das décadas, a estrutura cresceu, novos serviços foram incorporados e a medicina avançou. Um dos marcos recentes dessa trajetória foi a inauguração, em fevereiro de 2025, do Centro Madre Teresa de Jesus Gerhardinger, com 17.238 metros quadrados distribuídos em nove pavimentos, ampliando a capacidade de atendimento da instituição.

Na mesma igreja que acolheu as Irmãs pioneiras em 1936, a instituição celebrou nove décadas de dedicação à vida — Foto: Divulgação/Hospital São José

Mas, ao completar 90 anos, o Hospital São José celebra principalmente as pessoas que dão sentido à sua existência. Das Irmãs Escolares de Nossa Senhora, que deram início à missão, aos profissionais que hoje fazem parte da instituição, cada geração contribuiu para escrever essa história.

Após o encerramento da missa, os participantes foram convidados a compartilhar um bolo comemorativo pelos 90 anos do Hospital São José.

articles.title: The new international food pyramid: Plants and healthy carbs first; where do animal products fit?
articles.summary: Remember the time when we read about the food pyramid in our textbooks, with an image showing what laid where in the pyramid?
articles.body: Remember the time when we read about the food pyramid in our textbooks, with an image showing what laid where in the pyramid? Well, welcome to the new era of healthy eating, as the internationally developed food pyramid turns old wisdom upside down. Gone are the days when bread, rice, and pasta stood as the foundation of the ideal diet. Now, plants and quality carbs take center stage, while animal products step into supporting roles.Nutrition science, like everything else, evolves. For decades, people were told to load up on starchy carbs, then suddenly carbs became the villain. Now, as lifestyle diseases, diabetes, and climate worries force new thinking, the focus shifts yet again. A fresh International Food Guide Pyramid, hashed out by experts from places as different as Canada, China, the US, and the Nordic countries, aims to clear the confusion.What is the new International Food Guide Pyramid?Published in Advances in Nutrition in late September 2026, the International Food Guide Pyramid doesn’t just cherry-pick studies. Rather, it synthesizes findings from more than 250 scientific sources. It’s an evidence-informed dietary framework developed by researchers associated with the International Carbohydrate Quality Consortium (ICQC), led by Karen Della Corte of Brigham Young University in the US. It builds on current research and blends in ideas from the EAT-Lancet Planetary Health Diet, aiming for something that’s globally useful but flexible enough to adapt to different foods and cultures.What’s striking about the new pyramid is this: Plants are the foundation. The base layer is loaded with vegetables, fruits, seeds, nuts, beans, and whole grains. Meals should be built around these foods. Meat’s not banned, but it’s no longer the centerpiece. Red and processed meats move way up the pyramid, labeled as something to eat sparingly, while sources like fish and poultry get a “preferred” spot if you include animal products. Dairy and eggs are fine in moderate amounts, but again, plants are the real stars.Why go all in with plants?The science is convincing. Fiber, vitamins, minerals — all these come in abundance from produce, legumes, and nuts. There’s a clear link between eating more plant foods and better heart and metabolic health. Beans, lentils, tofu, and other soy products bring not just plant protein, but fiber and a bunch of micronutrients people often miss. Nuts and seeds pack protein, healthy fats, and fiber too.None of this means everyone’s expected to turn vegan. The point is to make plant foods the default: most of your plate comes from seeds, roots, and leafy stuff, not animal sources.The pyramid’s approach to carbohydrates is pretty refreshing. It stops short of telling people to shun carbs altogether. Instead, it insists on paying attention to carb quality. A bowl of white bread isn’t the same as whole barley or millet. The team looked at the glycemic index, which is the speed at which carbs spike blood sugar. Slow-release, high-fiber carbs like oats, brown rice, bulgur, and millets get a thumbs-up. Refined grains, sugary drinks, snacks — all these are pushed to the very top, marked as occasional treats at best.The guide recommends that at least half your grains come from “whole” sources and that you go for traditional, less-processed carbs when possible. This isn’t just about weight control; it’s a direct line to managing blood sugar and slashing risk for type 2 diabetes.Where do animal products fit?Pretty simply, they’re no longer leading the show. The new pyramid asks people to think of beans, nuts, and soy for protein, with fish and poultry as the top options among animal foods. Red meat and processed meats (think bacon, sausage, steak) are to be enjoyed rarely. Dairy and eggs can feature, but go for moderation. Fermented dairy (like yogurt and kefir) gets special mention for its benefits.What about fats?Out with the butter and lard, in with olive and canola oil, and more nuts, seeds, avocados. The advice is to flip your fat intake from animal to plant sources, not to cut out fat entirely. Again, it’s not about denying yourself, but picking smarter sources: less processed, more nutrients.Can this new pyramid really make a difference?The researchers behind it think so. They argue that a shift towards plant-forward eating could help prevent millions of early deaths tied to heart disease, diabetes, and other chronic illnesses, not to mention easing strain on the environment. Of course, it’s a framework, not a turnkey guarantee. Access to healthy food still depends heavily on where people live, what’s affordable, and what cultures and traditions shape everyday meals.After all, the new International Food Guide Pyramid boils everything down to one idea: Eating well isn’t about demonizing carbs, banning animal products, or getting caught up in endless protein fads. It’s about filling your plate with more diverse plants, reaching for whole, fiber-rich carbs, and swapping in healthy fats and proteins most of the time.Maybe the simplest mindset shift is this: Instead of asking, “How much meat or protein does this meal have?” try, “How many types of vegetables, grains, beans, or lentils are here?” That’s where the future of eating — not just healthier, but maybe tastier and more sustainable — really begins.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Lung cancer: Screening may have picked up my lung cancer earlier
articles.summary: Joan McConville is calling for a national screening programme in Northern Ireland, like there is in England and Wales.
articles.body:
"To the day I die, I will regret putting a cigarette in my mouth".

These are the words of Joan McConville, who was first diagnosed with lung cancer in 2023.

The former teacher believes her cancer may have been caught earlier if screening had been available in Northern Ireland.

Despite growing evidence that early detection can significantly reduce death rates, Northern Ireland has yet to fund a targeted lung cancer screening programme.

Although the Department of Health previously committed to introducing screening by April 2027, it has now confirmed there was "no definitive timeline" for its full implementation because of funding.

Smoking is the biggest risk factor for lung cancer , although genetic and environmental factors can also contribute.

McConville, from Banbridge, started smoking at 19 while studying in Belfast and said she became addicted to nicotine.

"It's not that my generation didn't know the dangers of cancer. We did," she said.

"We started smoking because it was trendy. And I enjoyed it."

The mother-of-three tried "really hard" to stop smoking, particularly during her pregnancies, but "never succeeded completely".

She also struggled to quit after her diagnosis, despite being referred to a smoking cessation clinic.

The 71-year-old said she "was not remotely surprised" by her diagnosis, having smoked for almost 50 years and having a family history of cancer.

After several months of coughing - one of the symptoms of lung cancer - she was admitted to Craigavon Area Hospital (CAH) following a "dreadful coughing fit".

A scan to check for a clot revealed a 3cm (1in) lesion in her right lung. While surgery successfully removed the cancer, it returned earlier this year.

McConville initially had scans every six months but said more than a year had passed when she developed pain in the upper right side of her chest.

Initially dismissing it as an injury from gardening or housework, she said the "tiny little niggle" became increasingly severe along with "dreadful" nausea.

The symptoms eventually made it difficult to go into town, walk or visit her grandchildren.

Following another visit to CAH, further scans showed the cancer had returned and spread to her lymph nodes and ribs.

Surgery was no longer an option, but radiotherapy and chemotherapy were recommended.

McConville believes regular screening could have led to earlier treatment and surgery, potentially improving her outcome.

"If my cancer had developed between the ages of 50 and 70, which it did, then there's every possibility that it would have been found earlier," she said.

"I was a smoker. I probably would still have got cancer. If I could have had screening and it could have made a difference to me, that would make me angry."

She said many people underestimate the risks, believing lung cancer happens to others.

She said screening would have brought that message home.

"If it was pointed out at a very early stage to smokers like me, 'Look that tiny little dot is cancer. Stop smoking now and we'll hopefully be able to remove it and then that's it gone'," she added.

Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths in Northern Ireland, with about 1,370 people diagnosed each year, according to Queen's University Belfast figures.

In 2022, the UK National Screening Committee recommended targeted screening across all four UK nations for people aged 55 to 74 who are at high risk of developing lung cancer, including current or ex-smokers.

Screening uses low-dose CT scans to identify lung cancer before symptoms develop.

England has begun rolling out screening, with full national coverage expected by 2030.

According to NHS England figures, nearly 13,000 lung cancers have been detected as a result with about three-quarters found at an early stage (stage 1 and 2) when cancer is most treatable.

Wales has announced a national programme , with the first invitations now expected in 2028.

While Scotland does not have a programme yet, it has been carrying out pilots .

Respiratory consultant Wendy Anderson leads Northern Ireland's lung cancer network.

She said while survival rates had been "increasing year on year, they're still not good".

"When I first started working as a consultant, less than one in 10 of our patients would have survived five years and now we're probably around one in four," she said.

Lung cancer is often diagnosed at a late stage where there are fewer treatment options available, meaning lower survival rates.

Anderson said screening could increase the proportion of people eligible for curative treatment from about 30% to 80%.

She estimated it could mean an additional 100 people a year surviving lung cancer or avoiding it altogether.

Screening could also tackle health inequalities by improving outcomes for people from more deprived communities, she added.

The respiratory consultant said reducing smoking rates remained the most important way to prevent lung cancer.

She added that stopping smoking not only reduced the chance of getting lung cancer, but also other respiratory diseases as well as heart attacks and strokes.

In December 2024, the former health minister Mike Nesbitt published a three-year health and social care plan to stabilise, reform and deliver services in Northern Ireland.

It said that "by April 2027, subject to additional funding, we will have a new targeted lung screening programme".

But now the Department of Health has said there is "no definitive timeline" for full implementation of the programme, as this will depend on future health funding.

It has funded a Public Health Agency (PHA) project team to assess what resources and funding are needed to deliver screening.

Planning will begin in December 2026 and is expected to take around a year.

articles.title: Aggressive cancer type linked to common chemical exposure in new study
articles.summary: A new NIH study links PFOA and PFOS forever chemicals to a 67% and 93% higher rate of ER-negative breast cancer, raising urgent questions. Experts weigh in.
articles.body: Two "forever chemicals" have been associated with a higher risk of aggressive breast cancer, according to research from the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Forever chemicals, known as PFAS, are a group of synthetic chemicals that break down extremely slowly and can build up in the environment and the human body. PFAS have been used in nonstick cookware, upholstery and clothing, as well as some food packaging and personal care items. CANCER RISK MAY BE HIGHER FOR PEOPLE WITH ONE PARTICULAR TYPE OF JOB The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, found that women with higher blood levels of two types of PFAS — perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) — were more likely to develop estrogen receptor-negative (ER-negative) breast cancer. ER-negative breast cancers tend to be "more aggressive" and have worse outcomes compared to breast cancers that respond to estrogen, according to a U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) press release. Data was drawn from a large U.S. research project called the Sister Study, which investigated environmental and genetic factors related to breast cancer. All participants had a sister diagnosed with breast cancer at enrollment but did not have breast cancer themselves. Researchers measured 17 PFAS in blood samples collected before diagnosis from 1,609 women who later developed breast cancer and a comparison sample of 2,269 women, then examined links between PFAS levels and breast cancer risk by tumor type. EATING LESS OF COMMON INGREDIENT EARLY IN LIFE MAY SLASH CANCER RISK DECADES LATER The highest PFOA exposure group had a 67% higher rate of ER-negative breast cancer. The rate was 93% higher in the highest PFOS group compared to those in the lowest group. These figures represent relative differences between groups, not an individual woman’s chance of developing breast cancer. "We know little about how they may influence health outcomes." The researchers found no clear association between PFOA or PFOS and breast cancer overall. "This study, along with the accompanying meta-analysis of previous studies, provides evidence that two PFAS are related to a higher ER-negative breast cancer risk," study leader Alexandra White, Ph.D., a researcher at the National Institutes of Health, told Fox News Digital. As this study focused mainly on older PFAS chemicals that have been largely phased out, the researcher said experts know "very little" about the PFAS that are replacing them, which could serve as a limitation. MICROPLASTICS DETECTED IN MOST HEART ATTACK PATIENTS' BLOOD IN STARTLING NEW STUDY "They tend to be shorter-chain compounds and may be less persistent in our bodies and the environment, but we know little about how they may influence health outcomes, such as breast cancer," she said. The findings show an association, not proof of causation, between forever chemical exposure and breast cancer risk, as the authors noted that more research is needed. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said that "women deserve clear answers about how chemicals in their environment may affect their health," calling for further investigation. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Under President Trump’s leadership, we will pursue the evidence, confront environmental health risks and give women the information they need to protect their health," he said. Medical oncologist Dr. Tiffany Troso-Sandoval, a New York City-based breast and gynecological cancer specialist who worked at Memorial Sloan Kettering for more than 25 years, also acknowledged that forever chemicals can increase cancer risk. "Oftentimes, once you've been exposed to them, they will accumulate in your body and cause havoc, and can actually increase the risk of carcinogenic transformation of cells," she told Fox News Digital. "What was interesting about this study is that the link was found only in ER-negative breast cancers, which is a known aggressive subtype of cancer." Few risk factors beyond genetic predispositions are known for ER-negative breast cancer, Troso-Sandoval noted, adding that "the study did not show that it increased the risk of all breast cancers in general." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ She suggested PFAS might damage DNA or interfere with the body's ability to repair that damage or destroy cancerous cells. While patients with ER-negative breast cancer had higher levels of these compounds in their bodies, that does not prove the chemicals caused their cancers, according to Troso-Sandoval. Reducing PFAS exposure First author Che-Jung Chang, Ph.D., a former research fellow at NIH and a current researcher at DLH, noted that although PFAS are "persistent" in the environment and in the human body, exposure is "potentially modifiable." "People can take steps to reduce their exposure, and these findings could open new avenues for prevention," she said. Troso-Sandoval recommends reviewing everyday sources of exposure to PFAS and other potentially harmful chemicals, including the following: Her concerns about black plastic utensils involve other chemical contaminants, including flame retardants. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Try to look at the products that you are using very frequently, and those are the first ones to swap out," she advised. "Maybe consider cooking with stainless steel pots and pans ... I recommend not heating up any food in plastic containers, because as you heat these plastics, they tend to leach more of the compounds into our foods." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP She recommends reviewing cosmetics and personal care products that may contain some of these compounds.

articles.title: 4 Ways to Make Your Walk More Challenging That Also Promote Healthy Aging
articles.summary: In TODAY.com’s Expert Tip of the Day,
articles.body: Walking isn’t just a way to get from point A to point B. It’s also one of the best activities we can do for our health, especially as we get older. It’s free, accessible, low-impact and you can do it anywhere. “Walking is a tremendous way that you can improve your fitness, even if you’re starting from zero,” Dr. Vonda Wright, an orthopedic surgeon, tells TODAY.com. Contrary to popular belief, walking can be a good workout. And science shows it can boost longevity, too. However, if your walks are feeling too easy, it may be time to tweak your routine and dial up the intensity. Here are Wright’s favorite ways to make walking more challenging to reap more benefits and promote healthy aging: Fitness Tip of the Day: Increase the Duration, Speed, Weight or Incline on Your Walk If you’re just starting a walking routine, “get off the couch and just take a walk, (ideally) after your biggest meal,” says Wright. Aim to walk at a moderate-intensity pace for at least 30 minutes, about five days of the week. “When that gets easy, we need to progressively overload our walk,” says Wright. This means dialing up the intensity of walking to make it more challenging on the body. You can do this in several ways, Wright says: Walk for a longer time or distance.Walk at a faster speed.Walk at an incline.Add weight to your walks. Why It Matters Walking on its own is a good form of aerobic exercise and an excellent way to promote longevity. Research shows that walking for as little as 11 minutes per day can reduce the risk of chronic disease and extend your lifespan, TODAY.com reported previously. However, using the principle of progressive overload can transform your walk into a more challenging workout with more benefits, including endurance, strength and longevity. Progressive overload means gradually increasing the amount of time, weight or intensity of a workout to challenge the body. Walking for a longer time or distance, for example, will help the body switch into exercise mode and burn more calories, TODAY.com reported previously. In the long run, it may lower the risk of death from all causes and boost longevity, studies show. Increasing the speed of your walk requires your heart to pump faster and your lungs to work harder — over time, going faster can improve endurance and cardiovascular health. Adding weight places more stress on the body and challenges the muscles, forcing them to adapt by growing stronger and larger. Increasing resistance or impact can also help improve or maintain bone density, which is crucial for healthy aging. How to Get Started If you’re new to walking or fitness, Wright recommends working gradually up to your desired time. “Start with five minutes, then 10 minutes and work up to 30 minutes,” she says. Once you get into a comfortable 30-minute walking routine, Wright recommends changing one variable at a time to make your walk more challenging. Once you adapt, change another variable, and continue this process. Here are some examples to get you started: Aim to walk for 10 more minutes or 1,000 more steps.Increase your pace to a brisk walk (3-4 mph) or try the interval walking method.Wear a 20-pound weighted vest, carry light dumbbells or use ankle weights.Walk up hills outside or increase the incline on a treadmill. Always consult to your doctor before changing your exercise routine, especially if you have any underlying health conditions or previous injuries. TODAY’s Expert Tip of the Day series is all about simple strategies to make life a little easier. Every Monday through Friday, different qualified experts share their best advice on diet, fitness, heart health, mental wellness and more.

articles.title: Irritable Male Syndrome Is Real — And It Might Be To Blame For Your Relationship Struggles
articles.summary: Decreasing testosterone levels in midlife can cause a host of physical and emotional issues in men.
articles.body:
Hormonal changes are a normal part of many phases of life ― for both women and men. Yet one is talked about more than the other. (We'll let you guess which one.)

One example? Hormonal changes in middle-aged men are often brushed off as a "midlife crisis," but experts say that couldn't be further from the truth. For men in their 40s or 50s, hormonal changes (such as a testosterone decrease) along with societal pressures can lead to a range of physical and emotional symptoms, said James Davis , a coaching psychologist and owner of Midlife Mentors in the U.K.

"Irritable male syndrome" is a condition that describes the drop in testosterone and other hormonal changes that can happen as men age. It is not a clinical diagnosis but is a recognized issue that was named by Scottish scientist Gerald Lincoln.

This time in life is more formally known as andropause, according to Davis. (This is the term Davis prefers.) "I think the serious side of this is a lot of men are adversely affected with their psychological health," Davis said.

Andropause is a time of increased anxiety, lower confidence, worries about midlife accomplishments and more. These issues impact men on a day-to-day basis and can add major stress in partnerships.

Ahead, experts break down exactly how issues related to low testosterone can impact relationships:

"If your testosterone is lowered, you can be more anxious [and] less confident," Davis said. "Then, if we layer on that, it's midlife and we start asking ourselves existential questions about, 'Am I where I wanted to be?' 'Is this what I have planned?' 'What's next for me?' It questions our whole sense of identity about who we are and what our place is in the world."

Mood changes are common during this time, said Mykal Manswell , a licensed professional counselor with Thriveworks. In addition to anxiety, depression can become more prevalent in middle-aged men, too, Manswell said.

In a relationship, anxiety, depression and lower confidence can show up in many ways — perhaps anxiety spirals that you talk out with your partner or a lower mood that means fewer date nights with your partner.

"It varies because everyone's human experience is different, but those are some of the statuses that we see, especially within the research as of lately," Manswell said.

"One that comes up all the time is intimacy, because we know it can be a really tricky time for both men and women," Davis said. "Libido can fluctuate, disappear." Erectile dysfunction issues can also happen at this time.

These issues can cause a "whole cascade of psychological triggers for men," he added. "And what they'll tend to do, sadly, is rather than try and talk about that, [they'll] withdraw."

Instead of withdrawing, Davis suggests talking to your partner about what's going on — and even finding a health professional who can help, too.

Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost .

3. Sleep Disruption, Which Can Lead To Lower Mood

Andropause and low testosterone can also cause sleep disruptions and loss of sleep.

"The relationship that you overall have with sleep, that is such a core contributing factor to your overall functionality as a human," Manswell said.

Poor sleep during midlife can lead to irritability and mood changes, he noted.

Traditionally, men haven't been encouraged to focus on their emotions and reach out for social support, said Kevin Ramotar , a clinical psychologist and the director of clinical product and AI at Grow Therapy .

"And we know that has been harmful," he noted, before adding that this is changing, but there is still a culture of suppressing emotions and not paying attention to underlying issues.

"But that becomes harder to do as you enter later life — maybe your kids are older ... the relationship issues that you've been tucking away and the resentment that you could have been building now starts to surface," he added. "You can only suppress things for so long until they come out."

This may come out as anger, sarcasm or irritability. "It's really just another form of externalizing depression, sadness," he said.

"I think as you move down the lifespan, in my opinion, the suppression gets weaker and it starts ... to come out, and it's harder to ignore, so you have that going on," he said.

In a relationship, this could look like snapping at your partner over issues that aren't serious or even pulling away if the resentment runs too deep.

As men age, muscle loss occurs, Manswell said. Your endurance can decline, too. Meaning, if you and your partner used to be avid exercisers or had a daily gym or walking routine, it may become harder to build up the motivation to stick to this.

The unfortunate reality is that this midlife low mood can turn into a "negative perpetuating cycle," Ramotar said.

"Where it's like — I need help, but I'm not asking for it. I'm pushing you away and then you step away from me," he said. In some cases, this negative cycle can result in late-life divorce.

While divorce is the right choice in some situations, seeking out mental health support can be a way to better communicate with your partner and understand what you're going through.

"You don't have to always wait until adversity hits to seek help," said Manswell, "and so the more preventative health measures that you can make, you might be able to catch things early on as well."

Mental health support is a big part of this, but so is physical health support.

"It's really when you start noticing the symptoms for a consistent period of time is when you should go and see your doctor ... a simple blood test will tell you what your testosterone levels are, and then you can look at your options," Davis said.

There are lifestyle adjustments that can help raise testosterone levels , Davis noted, such as getting good sleep, getting movement during the day, cutting out processed foods and more.

"There's a whole load of things we can do from a lifestyle perspective. If that's not working, then there is the option of testosterone replacement therapy, which is when ... we introduce testosterone to our system," Davis said.

This isn't an option for everyone, and it is a lifelong medical commitment, he said, but it is a good thing to be aware of.

If you're struggling with signs of andropause, it's worth talking to both mental health and physical health professionals, Manswell said. This can help you get back to feeling like you used to.

articles.title: Toukie Smith, ‘227’ Actor and Robert De Niro’s Former Partner, Dies After MS Battle: What to Know
articles.summary: Toukie Smith, a model and actor, has died at 74, the children she shared with Robert De Niro announced. Smith had multiple sclerosis, a nervous system disease.
articles.body: Toukie Smith, a model, actor and mother of twins with ex-partner Robert De Niro, died at 74, her children announced. The former “227” sitcom actor died on Nov. 4 after “a long, courageous battle with multiple sclerosis,” according to a statement released by her children, Airyn and Julian, whom she shared with De Niro. Smith was also the sister of legendary fashion designer Willi Smith, who died at 39 in 1987 from complications from AIDS. Toukie Smith also modeled for him, as well as for other luminaries like Hubert de Givenchy and Patrick Kelly. “As the sister of the late, legendary designer Willi Smith, Toukie shared in a remarkable family legacy that helped shape American fashion and culture,” her children wrote. “She was a model, muse and collaborator, not only to her beloved brother but to other trailblazing luminaries of the era, including the illustrator Alvaro, Jean-Paul Goude, Patrick Kelly and Antonio Lopez,” the statement continues. “Her beauty, grace and unmistakable presence helped pave the way for generations of Black models and designers in fashion.” Smith also played artist Eva Rawley on the hit NBC sitcom “227” starring Marla Gibbs, which ran from 1985 to 1990. She also appeared in multiple episodes of the classic ‘80s show “Miami Vice.” She and De Niro were partners from 1988 to 1996, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Airyn and Julian were conceived by in vitro fertilization and delivered by a surrogate mother. De Niro has five additional children with three other women. “Toukie was a force of nature,” her children wrote. “She left an indelible mark on our hearts and on everyone lucky enough to know her.” What Was Toukie Smith’s Cause of Death? The actor and model died following a “long” battle with multiple sclerosis, according to a statement by her two children. It’s not clear how long she had the autoimmune condition, but her children said in their statement that she died after a “long, courageous battle.” What Is Multiple Sclerosis? Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune condition that affects your central nervous system due to your immune system mistakenly attacking the protective sheaths that surround the nerves in your brain and spinal cord, according to Cleveland Clinic. There are almost a million adults in the United States living with the condition, per the Cleveland Clinic. Symptoms of MS include the following: Double vision or vision lossMuscle weaknessNumbness or abnormal sensationsFatigueLoss of balance or coordinationMuscle stiffness and spasmsDifficulty with memory, concentration, learning and judgmentMood changesDizzinessDifficulty regulating bladder There isn’t a single tool to diagnose someone with MS, which can sometimes make detecting it difficult for doctors. “It can take time before you receive an official MS diagnosis,” according to the Cleveland Clinic. “You may need to make several trips to see your provider before you know for sure. This happens because MS symptoms can look like or happen with several other common conditions.” While there is no cure for multiple sclerosis, there are treatments available to minimize symptoms and flare-ups. Still, MS can lead to disability, especially over time, and can be fatal in rare cases, according tot he Cleveland Clinic.

articles.title: Hysterectomy test revealed Coventry woman's rare cancer
articles.summary: Mum-of-four Donna Marklew, from Coventry, discovered she had cancer after a post-op biopsy.
articles.body:
Donna Marklew had to undergo a hysterectomy to treat complications caused by childbirth.

But the operation led the Coventry mum to receive a life-changing diagnosis when tests later revealed she had a rare form of cancer.

She was diagnosed with neuroendocrine cancer , which was only discovered after tissue removed during a hysterectomy at Warwick Hospital was analysed following a uterine prolapse.

"I was very shocked because I'd never heard of neuroendocrine cancer," she said.

"[I] was left with not much information because it wasn't known to anybody, and then trying to explain to people [that] I've been diagnosed with neuroendocrine cancer, you're kind of met with blank faces."

The rare cancer, which starts in the nerve and cell glands that make and release hormones, is estimated to affect 6,000 people in the UK every year, according to the charity, Neuroendocrine Cancer UK.

Lisa Walker, the chief executive of Neuroendocrine Cancer UK, said that the average time between people experiencing a first symptom and getting a diagnosis is five years.

"That is because the symptoms could be other conditions, and then people find themselves perhaps going down a different route and then needing to go back when the symptoms change or other symptoms are added in, which then start to look more like neuroendocrine cancer," she explained.

Marklew is now trying to raise awareness of the disease, which coincides with World Neuroendocrine Cancer Day on Tuesday.

She said that the disease is actually a group of cancers that develop in hormone-producing cells throughout the body.

Diagnosis can be particularly difficult, especially for women, she added.

Marklew, an occupational therapist who works in Leicestershire, said that after she was diagnosed, scans revealed tumours were discovered in her appendix, Fallopian tubes and surrounding tissue.

In March 2025, she underwent a nine hour surgery at Warwick Hospital to remove as many tumours as possible.

However, surgery alone has not been enough, and Marklew has to have three injections every week to try and keep the cancer under control.

She has also just started Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy (PRRT) which is administered four times a week, every two months.

"The tumours are slow growing, which is one of the benefits of this type of cancer.

"There's a different type of neuroendocrine as well, which can be more aggressive. but fortunately for me, mine are grade two, which means that they grow quite slowly, although mine are still growing."

However, Marklew, 44, said while she is able to live a normal life during her treatment, the disease has had a huge mental impact.

"'I've got four young children and my husband, my mum and my friends, and I think the reason why I've really wanted to get up and shout about it is because I just don't want anyone to have people feel so vulnerable when you find out that you have this diagnosis because nobody knows about it [the condition]."

Walker added: "It's a complex and diverse cancer and can develop in any part of the body, which is one of the things that makes detection difficult.

"It develops in the neuroendocrine cells. They produce and release the hormones that essentially regulate our different body functions and are found throughout the body.

"So it can affect any organ. Most commonly it does affect the lungs, the digestive tract, and the pancreas, but it can be found anywhere."

Marklew said that prior to her hysterectomy, she had no identifiable symptoms, although looking back, she thinks a trip to Scotland may have been an indicator.

"I was anxious and had palpitations during a trip to St Andrews for my first wedding anniversary, but my GP suggested that was down to me being perimenopausal."

She said unlike other cancers, because neuroendocrine is not as obvious or as widely known as others, few people understand how she feels.

"I could talk to my friends and family all day long, but no one will understand what it is like to live with this condition.

"It's really really hard and because it's invisible everybody will say - oh you look great."

She said she reached out to the charity Neuroendocrine UK for support and advice.

"They're an absolutely invaluable resource for people that have been diagnosed and they have patient groups in other areas, so I said I'd really like to set one up.

"We did one in September and one other person came along, which was nice because it was a nice opportunity for me and her to have a couple of hours conversation along with one of the nurses as well.

"Then we [did] it bi-monthly, we had six people and it felt so good".

articles.title: Is It Healthy To Eat Canned Tuna Every Day? A Dietitian Weighs In
articles.summary: Eating fish frequently is good for your heart and brain. But is canned tuna healthy enough to eat every single day? A dietitian reveals the best options.
articles.body: Canned tuna feels like a cheat code for high-protein meals. It’s affordable, easy to transport and packed with filling, healthy nutrients. But is tuna healthy enough to eat every single day? As healthy as this food is, there are some important concerns to keep in mind if you want to eat canned tuna that frequently, dietitians say. “Tuna is an excellent source of high-quality protein, and it provides nutrients including vitamin B12, selenium and omega-3 fatty acids,” explains Natalie Rizzo, registered dietitian and TODAY nutrition editor. And canned tuna is an especially “affordable and accessible way to eat more seafood,” she adds. But tuna, particularly some varieties of canned tuna, can be higher in mercury than other types of fish. And certain products may also come with flavorings that add large amounts of sodium. That doesn’t mean you need to avoid canned tuna, Rizzo says, but there are some factors to consider if you want to eat it frequently. Is It Healthy To Eat Canned Tuna Every Day? There are a lot of great reasons to incorporate canned tuna into your diet. For starters, it’s an incredibly efficient source of protein, packing about 22 grams in a 3-ounce serving, TODAY.com explained previously. In tuna, you’ll also find healthy omega-3 fatty acids, including the type of brain-healthy fats that are unique to marine food sources, including fish. Additionally, the American Heart Society recommends getting at least two servings of fish every week, a quota many people in the U.S. do not meet. Canned tuna is an easy, affordable way to help meet that goal. But if you love canned tuna enough to eat it every single day, know that there are some health concerns with consuming it that frequently, Rizzo says. “The biggest concern with eating tuna frequently is mercury, and the amount varies substantially depending on the species,” she says. Canned light tuna tends to be lower in mercury, while albacore or white tuna is a larger fish and contains significantly more mercury, Rizzo notes. Yellowfin tuna also has more mercury than light tuna, and bigeye tuna is among the highest-mercury fish. Typically, canned tuna labeled as “light” is primarily skipjack tuna, which dietitians previously told TODAY.com is the healthiest variety of canned tuna. Other canned tuna varieties can still be part of a healthy diet, but should be eaten less frequently than skipjack. If You Want To Eat Tuna Frequently… The Food and Drug Administration recommends that people who are pregnant or breastfeeding, as well as children age 11 and under, limit the amount of fish they eat. Generally, the FDA’s advice is to eat no more than two to three 4-ounce servings of fish per week for adults and no more than two servings per week for children, with smaller serving sizes for younger kids. For other adults who want to eat more than three servings of fish per week, the FDA recommends eating a variety of fish from the agency’s list of best choices (which includes skipjack tuna). “The amount of mercury in the fish matters most for pregnant people and children,” Rizzo notes. “If you’re eating tuna (a lot), then you should choose lower mercury options. However, if you have it once or twice a week, choose the variety that you enjoy most.” Choose a Lower-Mercury Type of Tuna The amount of mercury in canned tuna can vary widely depending on the type of fish. If you want to eat tuna frequently, opt for canned light tuna, including skipjack, which the FDA lists as one of the best choices for fish. Opt for Tuna Packed With Ingredients That Are Right for You Canned tuna can be packed with all sorts of ingredients. When it comes to oil versus water, know that tuna packed in oil has a richer flavor and comes with more calories and fat. Meanwhile, tuna packed with water tends to be lower in calories and has the plainest flavor and texture. “I’m a big fan of tuna packed in (extra virgin olive oil) because it really doesn’t need anything else added to it to taste great,” registered dietitian Frances Largeman-Roth told TODAY.com previously. But if calories are your primary concern, tuna packed in water may be a better choice. However, Rizzo recommends avoiding tuna packed with added salt or other flavorings. Instead, add your own additional herbs, spices and ingredients to make a more complete, nutritious meal. For instance, try making tuna salad with plain Greek yogurt for an additional protein boost. Vary Your Seafood Choices There’s nothing wrong with eating fish frequently. In fact, it’s a healthy, nutritious choice that boosts brain health. But if you want to eat fish more than three times per week, try to vary the types of low-mercury seafood you’re incorporating in your meals to get a variety of nutrients. “For the general adult population, I recommend eating a variety of fish, rather than eating tuna seven days a week,” Rizzo says. “Rotate tuna with lower-mercury seafood, such as salmon, sardines, shrimp and trout, as well as plant proteins.”
